subject: Private endpoint connectivity — control-plane proxy handover and egress ownership
messages:
From: netcorp-security@netcorp.com
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: partner-cloudops@netcorp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private endpoint requirements for upcoming on‑prem deployment

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

We're kicking off the security review for NetCorp's planned private deployment of Redwood in our on‑prem environment. Attached is our current requirements doc — highlights and asks below:

- Hard requirement: all outbound connections from the private connector must exit via our perimeter proxy (TLS passthrough preferred) and be allowlisted by destination IP(s).
- We will only allow static egress IPs (a /29 preferred) for third‑party services. Can Redwood provide a minimal set of IPs to allow?
- Control plane heartbeat: we need the connection frequency and expected ports so our WAF teams can set sensible timeouts.
- mTLS is desired between our proxy and Redwood control plane. If Redwood does not support mTLS, we need a plan for cert pinning + rotation.
- DNS behavior: with split‑horizon DNS in our environment, we need guidance on whether Redwood requires public DNS resolution or if we can route to an internal VIP.

Please confirm an owner at Redwood who will take the proxy / egress handoff, and any docs you can share (IP lists, runbook, automation) so we can start firewall rules and change windows.

Attachments: netcorp_private_deploy_requirements_v1.pdf (security checklist)

Thanks,
NetCorp Security Team
netcorp-security@netcorp.com

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: netcorp-security@netcorp.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, partner-cloudops@netcorp.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint requirements for upcoming on‑prem deployment

Hi — thanks for the clear list, appreciate the doc. Looping in our ops lead (Marissa) and infra (Dev) to cover runbook and port specifics. Quick responses inline: 

- Static egress IPs: Redwood can publish a small set of static egress IPs for control‑plane interactions (management/metrics/updates). See attached redwood-egress-ips.csv — these IPs are for control plane only.
- Data‑plane traffic (inference requests) can be configured to stay entirely in your VPC/to your internal NAT if you prefer; if Redwood endpoints are used, we can provide dedicated IPs or an internal peering option depending on the Private plan.
- mTLS: we support mTLS for control plane; we will require a CSR/thumbprint exchange during onboarding. If you cannot do mTLS right away, we can use TLS with certificate pinning as an interim step.
- DNS: we support both public DNS and split‑horizon setups. If you host an internal VIP for the connector, we can accept that as long as the cert SNI matches.

I'll attach our proposed handoff runbook (runbook-egress-handoff.md) and suggest a live handoff call early next week to lock the change window. Who should own the actual proxy config on your side? We recommend NetCorp run the perimeter proxy and NAT, and Redwood will own the control‑plane cert rotation and our connector's health checks.

Next step: proposed call slots 2026‑12‑13 1400–1600 PST or 2026‑12‑14 0900–1100 PST. Please confirm.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Vanessa. A couple of clarifying questions from the ops side:

1) If NetCorp routes inference traffic through their perimeter proxy (TLS passthrough), will they preserve SNI? We rely on SNI for routing to dedicated model pools in some topologies. If SNI is stripped, we need a different routing plan.

2) Heartbeat frequency: we need to define acceptable ranges. For most customers we do a 30s keepalive and a 2m health probe window before failover. Is NetCorp comfortable with that?

3) Ports: please confirm whether outbound-only 443 is acceptable, or if you need specific ephemeral ports opened.

Dev — can you validate and add the exact port/IP list and any iptables rules we recommend?

Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

From: dev.patel@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: netcorp-security@netcorp.com
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private endpoint requirements for upcoming on‑prem deployment

Marissa — notes from infra/ops. I put specifics below and attached an automation bundle (egress_automation_playbook.zip) with iptables snippets and a small cert exchange helper.

Summary (technical):
- Ports: outbound TCP/443 only to the control‑plane IPs in redwood‑egress‑ips.csv. Data plane (if you are using Redwood hosted endpoints) also uses 443 to the model pool IPs; we explicitly do not require additional ephemeral ports.
- Heartbeat: client keepalive (TLS-level) every 30s; application ping every 60s. Our control plane tolerates 3 missed pings before marking unhealthy (approx 3–4 minutes).
- mTLS: control plane CN = controlplane.redwood.internal (we'll provide CA bundle). SNI must be preserved if you rely on SNI-based routing; if your TLS termination breaks SNI we recommend TLS passthrough or TCP NAT at the perimeter.
- NAT/eIP: For the handoff we can accept either (a) NetCorp provides static egress IPs and routes outbound to our published IPs, or (b) NetCorp peers privately and uses internal IPs (requires a different onboarding workflow). Option (a) is quickest for firewall teams.
- Fallback: if control plane egress is blocked, connectors will buffer telemetry and metrics locally and attempt exponential backoff; we recommend an ops alert for >5m of no-controlplane connectivity.

Firewall rule example (short):
- action: allow
- proto: tcp
- source: 10.0.0.0/18 (connector subnet)
- dest: 34.201.125.10, 34.201.125.11, 34.201.125.12 (redwood control plane IPs)
- ports: 443

Attachments: egress_automation_playbook.zip (scripts and iptables snippets)

On the call I can run through a staged handoff: 1) NetCorp applies firewall rules to allow our control plane IPs, 2) we exchange CSR and verify mTLS, 3) we run a 30m connectivity test window, 4) we flip traffic and monitor.

— Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
